The implementation is complete and thoroughly validated.

## Summary

`/work/submission/main.py` (16 KB, stdlib-only, self-contained) implements:

**Strict input validation** â a `JSONDecoder` constructed with `object_pairs_hook` (duplicate-key rejection), `parse_constant` (NaN/Infinity rejection) and `parse_float` (float rejection), one-value decoding with strict JSON-whitespace trailing check, UTF-8 strictness, 2 MiB cap, plus full type/range checks (`type(x) is int` so booleans and floats fail), exact key sets, unique `(u,v)` pairs, drop-list validity, and the 8192-concrete-path bound (exact DAG DP count). Any violation prints exactly `{"error":"invalid-input"}` and exits 2.

**Discrete-event replay** â a heap keyed by `(time, priority, round ID, event key)` realizing the five-level priority order (releases â PING deliveries â ACK deliveries â timeouts â host ACKs). It models per-`(round,node)` cache entries, dedup with waiting-parent sets and immutable cached ACKs to finalized entries, capacity drops, late-PING discards, per-edge loss applied after transmission counting, proof-set union on ACK credit, conjunction-based completion, one-shot frozen finalization, per-round release at `deadline+1`, and source/host-ACK delivery that may land after cache release. Peaks are sampled at every allocation; `end_us` is the last processed event.

**Evidence analysis** â enumerates all full-graph sât edge paths, partitions them by label signature, and marks a signature observed in a round only when some complete path lies entirely inside that round's frozen source proof (per-round, never unioned across rounds), with lexicographic class ordering, witness selection, and the deterministic lower/upper bounds and coverage status.

Verification performed: exact match on `diamond.expected.json`; ~12 000 randomized differential cases against two independently structured implementations (heap vs. time-bucket batching, plus a third subgraph-reenumeration evidence checker); a 4 000-case structural/invariant schema checker; 92 boundary-validation cases; 900+ byte/structure mutation cases (never crashing, always valid JSON); event-uniqueness assertion over fuzzing; all limit boundaries (2 MiB Â± 1, 384/385 edges, 48/49 rounds, 8192/8193 paths); and worst-case performance (8192 paths, 96 nodes, 384 edges, 48 rounds â 0.75 s, 9.9 MB output) well inside the 120 s / 1 GiB / 32 MiB ceilings, with hash-seed-independent deterministic output.
